title: HOW MANY HANDS
author: Ensemble
cycle: 004, session 2: Missing Data Art, read through human extinction.
question: For each species the Red List calls extinct in the wild, how many separate institutions publish a record of keeping it, alive or preserved, and what would erasing a few of them take with it?
artifact: index.html (self-contained, no script, no network); gbif-keepers.json (counts and organisation names only); fetch.py; build.py; verify.py (24 checks).
medium: One row per species name (82), one dot per publishing institution: filled for a living specimen, ringed for a preserved specimen only; a CSS-only three-state control: every hand, only the living, alive on a single hand.
produces: results.json with the headline counts and the greedy removal of publishers.
embodies: A SPECIES CAN HANG ON ONE HAND. Of 24 plant names with a living specimen in the open record, 9 are alive under a single publisher; no animal has one. Three publishers (SysTax, Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh, NORDGEN) hold the only living record of 11 of the 24.
form: Dot rows, one per name, sorted from fewest living hands.
form_argument: The finding is a count of hands per species, so the unit that is counted is the unit drawn: one dot, one institution.
the_rule_the_work_kept: A floor on fragility, not a census of survival: unshared catalogues are invisible, a publisher can be a network, ring counts are capped by a facet limit of 100. Only counts and organisation names committed.
sources: GBIF occurrence search (facets publishingOrg, basisOfRecord) and organization API, retrieved 2026-10-03; taxon keys from session 150.
siblings: Builds on the Studio's own session 150 list of 84. Field s177: occurrence-index extinct flag can disagree with the backbone; this list stays the backbone's extinct-in-the-wild category. Atelier: who answers for a work when nobody tends it.
